text: ITR-3 is applicable to individuals and HUFs having income from business or profession, including partners in a firm.
Taxpayers with income from proprietary business, professional practice, or partnership firms must file ITR-3.
Enter PAN, Aadhaar, address, nature of business or profession, and filing status accurately as per official records.
This section captures details of income from proprietary business or profession, including turnover, expenses, and net profit.
Select the appropriate nature of business or profession code applicable to your activity.
Provide details of gross receipts, expenses, depreciation, and net profit as per books of accounts.
Report assets and liabilities as at year end, including capital account, loans, and fixed assets.
Report salary income, if any, received in addition to business or professional income.
Declare income or loss from house property, including interest on housing loan.
Report short-term and long-term capital gains from sale of capital assets such as shares, property, or mutual funds.
Include income such as interest, dividends, family pension, or other taxable receipts.
Partners in firms should report share of profit, remuneration, interest, and capital balance details.
Resident taxpayers must disclose foreign assets, foreign income, and signing authority in applicable schedules.
Schedule FA requires disclosure of foreign bank accounts, financial interests, and foreign trusts.
Schedule AL captures assets and liabilities if total income exceeds the specified threshold.
Claim deductions under Chapter VI-A such as 80C, 80D, 80G, and other applicable sections.
Tax liability is computed based on total income, slab rates, surcharge, cess, and applicable rebates.
Report tax deducted or collected at source as per Form 16, 16A, and Form 26AS.
Provide advance tax and self-assessment tax payment details including challan information.
Provide details of all bank accounts held and select one account for receiving refund.
If business turnover exceeds prescribed limits, maintaining books of accounts and audit details is mandatory.
Enter audit report details if accounts are audited under the Income-tax Act or other applicable laws.
Verify the return using e-verification methods or submit ITR-V within the prescribed time to complete filing.
The return becomes invalid if verification is not completed within the allowed time after submission.
